mn115:12.7: These first three paragraphs on the possible and impossible clearly show the difference between an Arahant, whose view is perfected, and an ordinary person, who has not gone beyond self-view.
mn115:13.9: See Sutta 38 and the note there.
mn115:14.1: The elder Nāgasena, in the Milindapañhā, states that two Buddhas do not arise in one world in order to prevent quarrelling among their unenlightened disciples.
mn115:15.1: Women can become Arahants, as many did in the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha, but no example is known of a woman originally discovering the Dhamma as a Fully Enlightened Buddha.
mn115:18.1: The reservation ‘because of that, for that reason’ is explained in Sutta 136.
